Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

BEGIN REFERENCE NOTES
The Mendez family began gathering its photographs in one place after Elena Mendez found three boxes in the hallway closet of her mother's apartment in Tacoma. The boxes held prints from family trips, school portraits, and envelopes of negatives; a fourth box contained CDs labeled in her father Luis's handwriting. Elena and her brother Rafael scanned the prints over two weekends in March. Their cousin Nina brought a flatbed scanner from her office and showed them how to save each scan as a TIFF master and a smaller JPEG for browsing. They agreed that the archive should make it easier to find pictures, rather than replace the boxes or the files already held by relatives.

Luis's CDs cover several years, but their labels are not a dependable guide to what is on them. One disc marked “Christmas 2008” contains a mix of holiday pictures and a school concert from January. A folder from Rafael's old laptop is named “Camera Roll,” and its files include dates from 2006 through 2011. Elena said, “The label can help us look, but it can’t be the date we trust.” The family wants the scanned prints to retain their envelope and approximate event information, while camera files should keep any reliable capture date recorded in their metadata. No one has yet checked every image or confirmed that all the old discs can be read.

During the first scan session, Nina noticed that some prints had dates written on the back in pencil. She photographed those backs as separate reference images and wrote the envelope name on a small card in the frame. A few prints have no date, and several envelopes say only “summer” or “visit.” Rafael’s phone pictures sometimes show the date they were copied rather than the day they were taken. Elena has started a spreadsheet with columns for filename, likely year, source box or device, and notes, but she has only entered the first two envelopes. The family does not want a guessed date to be treated as a verified capture date.

The relatives use different devices and do not all have the same internet connection. Elena keeps the working archive on a small external drive attached to her home computer. Rafael travels for work and has asked to browse selected JPEGs when he visits, but the family has not chosen a shared online service. Nina suggested that any configuration should distinguish the local archive from a browsing copy and should not silently send files elsewhere. Luis was concerned about the scans becoming difficult to retrieve after a computer change. “If the drive moves to a new computer, I still want the folders to make sense,” he said. The family has not tested a restore from the external drive.

The archive should keep the source material easy to recognize. The original filenames on camera images can be opaque, and multiple devices may produce the same filename. Elena prefers that a configuration preserve the source files and make organized copies rather than rename or move originals. For scanned prints, the envelope name and any known event should remain available alongside the scan. Rafael has mentioned that he may add pictures from his phone after each family gathering, while Nina expects to finish scanning the remaining boxes during the autumn. Neither has set a firm schedule for those additions.

1. The family has identified three useful kinds of information: a verified camera capture date, a date or event written on an envelope or print, and an uncertain estimate such as “summer.” Keep those distinctions visible. A written note or an estimate can help with browsing, but it is not confirmation of a camera capture date. When the source is unclear, retain that uncertainty instead of silently substituting a date.
2. Preserve the relationship between each organized copy and its source device, disc, box, or envelope wherever the configuration supports it. The source material includes TIFF scans, JPEG browsing copies, camera files, photographed print backs, and spreadsheet notes. The family has not completed its inventory, so the plan should work with additions without implying that all files have already been checked.
3. Elena wants the first setup to be understandable to relatives who are not comfortable with command-line tools. Nina can help with a one-time setup, but the family expects to use the result through ordinary folders afterward. Rafael asked that a review folder be easy to notice so uncertain dates do not disappear among dated pictures.

[local_archive]
retain_days = 18
allow_remote = false
name = "local-copy"

The family has not decided whether it will ever make an online browsing copy, and Rafael's request to browse selected pictures is only a suggestion for a later conversation. For the current setup, the external drive is the working location, and the supplied settings are the family's starting point rather than evidence that a backup or restore process has been tested. Elena plans to bring the spreadsheet to the next family visit so relatives can correct names and event notes together. Keep that unfinished work in view when preparing the configuration plan, and do not treat uncertain dates, unread discs, or the untested drive as settled matters.
